newsitem.title: USA: GM to hire 64 workers at Ohio truck plant.
newsitem.headline: GM to hire 64 workers at Ohio truck plant.

text.p: General Motors Corp agreed to hire about 64 more workers at its Moraine, Ohio, assembly plant and pay a $1,000 signing bonus to about 4,100 existing workers as part of a new local labor agreement, union officials said on Thursday.
Members of International Union of Electronics workers Local 801, who ended a three-day strike at the plant on Wednesday, are scheduled to vote on the pact Thursday and Friday.

The proposed contract also calls for GM to pay over $300,000 in grievance settlements and provide a 10 percent shift premium to the plant's so-called C-Crew, one of three production teams that rotate on two 10-hour daily shifts.
The plant produces compact four-door sport/utility vehicles, including the Chevrolet Blazer, GMC Jimmy and Oldsmobile Bravada.
The pact excludes tough penalties for absences, which caused workers to reject it last week, leading to a strike that started Sunday morning.
The local pact, which expires May 1, 2000, also calls for GM to give workers a $50 voucher toward the purchase of safety shoes in addition to five sets of uniforms per year.
In a statement, the union's chief GM negotiator, Harold Nichols, encouraged IUE members to vote for the pact.
